extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, organizations, and stakeholders who want to submit comments on New York City proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for submitting public comments on NYC proposed rules (how to post comments, what information is required, privacy considerations, deadlines, and alternate submission methods). Applies to comments submitted via the NYC Rules website and via agency-provided alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website comment submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To comment on a proposed rule, click on the “Add new comment” links next to the rules below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Add new comment' link beside each listed proposed rule to submit via the NYC Rules site. For alternate ways to submit (mail, fax, email), click on a proposed rule for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required commenter information
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit your name and email in order to leave a comment (your email address will not be published with your comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name and email are required fields for submitting a comment through the site. While the email address will not be published with the visible comment, it must be provided to submit the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spam review and posting delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comment will be reviewed for spam before it is posted on the site and may take up to one full business day to be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a moderation step for spam; allow up to one full business day for a submitted comment to appear publicly after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public visibility and public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that all comments are visible to the public once submitted and become public record once the commenting period closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are publicly viewable upon submission and, after the comment period closes, become part of the public record. Consider this when deciding what to include in your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy guidance — avoid including personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not wish for your personal information to be visible or become part of the public record, please do not include it in your comment or in any attachment submitted with your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal information may include your name, mailing address, or other details that are unique to you, such as what you do for a living. Do not put such details in comment text or attachments if you want to avoid public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: City agencies also accept comments by mail, fax, or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For agency-specific instructions on mail/fax/email submissions, click on the listing for the proposed rule in the table to view alternate submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadlines and hearing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted until the date indicated in the “Comment Deadline” column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proposed rule listing includes a 'Hearing Date' and a 'Comment Deadline' — you must submit comments by the listed deadline. Some entries show 'Comments Closed' when the period has ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Comment & Posting Policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are subject to the site's Comment & Posting Policy (linked on the page), which governs moderation, acceptable content, and posting rules. Review that policy for more detailed standards and restrictions.
